name: Filament severed at 1.4 times its critical length
question: Does the buckle survive a generation when the filament is severed close to its critical length?
assumptions: an inextensible wormlike chain in a plane, both ends on the axis of the load, free to slide along it and free to turn; ten rigid segments
units kappa = zeta_perp = 1, F = pi^2 (so that L_c = pi (kappa/F)^(1/2) = 1), zeta_par = zeta_perp/2

growth by uniform elongation at the rate 5, fast against the relaxation of the residual buckle (a viscous or crowded medium); for microtubules in water the residual relaxes about 1e4 times faster than the filament regrows
division by severing at 1.4 L_c: the regrowth above L_c does not restore what the dip removes (ln G < 0)
thermal noise k_B T = 1e-2 (reduced temperature t = L/(pi^2 L_p) of about 1e-3)

provenance.source: K. Baczynski, R. Lipowsky and J. Kierfeld, Phys. Rev. E 76, 061914 (2007), Eqs. 1-2, 6, 26; dynamics of O. Hallatschek, E. Frey and K. Kroy, Phys. Rev. E 75, 031905 (2007), Eqs. 8-11
